trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Check-In: Flight AC lands at 13:00, so morning is travel time. Head from the airport to your accommodation in Old Montreal via the 747 express bus (~$11 CAD) — the most budget-friendly airport transfer option.
day_by_day.afternoon: Old Montreal Orientation Walk: After checking in, take a self-guided stroll through the cobblestone streets of Vieux-Montréal. Visit Place Jacques-Cartier, admire the Notre-Dame Basilica exterior (free), and soak in the historic architecture along Rue Saint-Paul. Get your bearings and scout local spots for the days ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Old Montreal Culinary Walking Tour: Join an early-evening culinary walking tour through Vieux-Montréal, stopping at iconic spots for smoked meat sandwiches, local poutine, and Quebec-style treats. Many tours run around $25–40 CAD and cover multiple tastings, making it great value for a first-night food introduction.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and croissant at the airport or on arrival — skip a full breakfast since you land at 13:00.
meals.lunch: Pick up a quick and affordable smoked meat sandwich or bagel from a deli near Old Montreal (~$10–14 CAD) shortly after check-in.
meals.dinner: Tastings included in the culinary walking tour. Supplement with a cheap crepe or BeaverTail pastry from a street vendor in Place Jacques-Cartier (~$6–8 CAD).

day_by_day.notes: Take the 747 STM express bus from Trudeau Airport to downtown — it's the cheapest airport transfer at ~$11 CAD (includes 24h transit pass). Old Montreal is very walkable from your accommodation, so no additional transit needed this afternoon. Weather should be warm (~25°C), perfect for an outdoor stroll.

day_by_day.morning: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour: Head to Jean-Talon Market (take the Metro Orange Line to Jean-Talon station, ~$3.75 CAD). Explore one of North America's largest open-air markets, sampling Quebec cheeses, maple products, fresh fruits, and artisan breads. Graze your way through the stalls — this is both breakfast and a cultural experience. Budget ~$15–20 CAD for tastings and small purchases.
day_by_day.afternoon: Mile End Neighbourhood Exploration: Walk or bike (BIXI bike share, ~$7/day) through the trendy Mile End district. Visit the famous Fairmount Bagel or St-Viateur Bagel for a fresh Montreal bagel (~$2 CAD). Browse colourful murals, independent boutiques, and the vibrant multicultural street life on and around Boulevard Saint-Laurent.
day_by_day.evening: St-Laurent Boulevard Street Food Crawl: As the sun sets, dive into the iconic 'Main' for a self-guided street food crawl. Sample Portuguese chicken at Romados, grab Montreal-style hot dogs, and explore diverse cuisines from Lebanese shawarma to Québécois comfort food. Budget ~$20–25 CAD total for a satisfying progressive dinner.

meals.breakfast: Graze on free and low-cost samples at Jean-Talon Market — Quebec cheese, maple taffy, fresh fruit (~$5–8 CAD for extras).
meals.lunch: Fresh Montreal bagel with cream cheese from Fairmount or St-Viateur Bagel in Mile End (~$4–6 CAD). Pair with a coffee from a local café.
meals.dinner: St-Laurent Boulevard Street Food Crawl — mix and match from multiple vendors. Portuguese chicken at Romados, shawarma, or a classic hot dog (~$20–25 CAD total).

day_by_day.notes: A day Metro pass costs ~$11 CAD and is worth it if you plan multiple trips. BIXI bike share is a fun and cheap way to get between Mile End and St-Laurent. Jean-Talon Market is busiest and most vibrant in the morning, so arrive early (by 9:00–10:00 AM) for the best experience. Bring a reusable bag if you want to pick up market snacks for later.

day_by_day.morning: Just for Laughs Festival — Free Outdoor Performances: Head to the Just for Laughs (Juste pour rire) Festival hub around Rue Saint-Denis and Boulevard de Maisonneuve. The festival runs mid-July and features extensive FREE outdoor stages with comedy acts, street performers, and live entertainment. Arrive early to grab a good spot and enjoy the festive atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Festival Street Food & Plateau Mont-Royal Wander: Enjoy the festival's street food vendors for lunch, then walk north to explore the charming Plateau Mont-Royal neighbourhood. Admire the iconic outdoor staircases, colourful duplexes, and local parks. Visit Parc Lafontaine (~20 min walk from festival zone) for a relaxing picnic break — a beloved local green space that's completely free.
day_by_day.evening: Just for Laughs Evening Shows & Festival Atmosphere: Return to the festival for the evening programming. Free outdoor concerts and comedy performances ramp up after dark. Grab festival street food for dinner and enjoy the lively crowd. If you want a ticketed indoor show, budget seats can sometimes be found for ~$20–35 CAD — check the festival website for last-minute deals.

meals.breakfast: Pick up a fresh pastry and café au lait from a local bakery near your Old Montreal hotel (~$6–9 CAD). Try Olive + Gourmando or a nearby boulangerie.
meals.lunch: Festival street food vendors near the Just for Laughs stages — poutine, grilled corn, tacos, or Québécois snacks (~$12–16 CAD).
meals.dinner: Continue grazing at festival food stalls or grab a falafel wrap or shawarma from a nearby affordable restaurant on Rue Saint-Denis (~$12–15 CAD).

day_by_day.notes: Just for Laughs typically runs from mid-to-late July — confirm the exact 2027 dates and free show schedule at hahaha.com closer to your trip. The free outdoor programming is extensive and genuinely world-class, making this an incredible budget-friendly day. Bring a light layer for the evening as temperatures can drop slightly after sunset. Transit: Metro Green Line to Berri-UQAM station puts you right in the festival zone.

day_by_day.morning: Mount Royal Park Hike: Start the day with a free hike up Mont Royal — Montreal's iconic park designed by Frederick Law Olmsted (same designer as Central Park). The trail to the summit belvedere takes about 45–60 minutes and rewards you with a stunning panoramic view of the city skyline. Bring water and a snack from the previous day's market haul.
day_by_day.afternoon: Atwater Market & Lachine Canal Picnic: Take the Metro to Lionel-Groulx and walk to Atwater Market — a smaller but beloved covered market with excellent local vendors. Pick up artisan cheeses, charcuterie, fresh bread, and seasonal fruit for an affordable picnic lunch (~$15–20 CAD). Head to the adjacent Lachine Canal path, rent a BIXI bike, and cycle along the waterfront for a scenic and relaxing afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner in Old Montreal: Return to your home base in Vieux-Montréal for a final dinner. Try L'Avenue (brunch-style comfort food) or a BYOB (apportez votre vin) restaurant — Montreal is famous for its BYOB culture, where you can bring your own wine to many restaurants, dramatically reducing the bill. Pick up a bottle from a SAQ (liquor store) for ~$13–18 CAD and enjoy a proper sit-down meal without the markup.

meals.breakfast: Simple and cheap — grab a banana and granola bar before the hike, or stop at a café near the Mont Royal entrance for a coffee and muffin (~$5–7 CAD).
meals.lunch: DIY picnic assembled from Atwater Market: local cheese, baguette, charcuterie, and fruit eaten along the Lachine Canal (~$15–20 CAD total, very generous spread).
meals.dinner: BYOB restaurant in Old Montreal or Plateau area. Many offer table d'hôte (set menu) deals for ~$25–35 CAD per person including two or three courses — exceptional value. Pick up wine at SAQ beforehand (~$13–18 CAD).

day_by_day.notes: Mont Royal Park is entirely free and one of the best things to do in Montreal — don't miss it. The Lachine Canal bike path is flat, scenic, and family-friendly; BIXI bikes are available at multiple docking stations near Atwater Market. For the BYOB dinner, search 'apportez votre vin Montréal' to find a list of participating restaurants — it's a uniquely Montréal dining tradition and a brilliant budget hack. Check out of your accommodation the next morning; confirm late checkout if your departure flight allows.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Montreal Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Take a taxi or airport express bus (~45 min) to your Old Montreal hotel. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented with a leisurely stroll through the cobblestone streets of Vieux-Montréal to shake off travel fatigue.
day_by_day.afternoon: Old Montreal Culinary Walking Tour: Starting from your hotel, join an afternoon guided culinary walk through Vieux-Montréal. Stop at iconic spots for smoked meat sandwiches, local poutine, artisan chocolates, and Quebec-style bagels. Explore Place Jacques-Cartier and the Notre-Dame Basilica exterior along the way.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Old Port waterfront for a relaxed evening stroll along the Promenade du Vieux-Port. Enjoy the warm summer air and check out any live street performances happening near the waterfront amphitheatre, which often feature free entertainment in July.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and croissant at the airport or skip — you arrive at 13:00.
meals.lunch: Included as part of the Old Montreal Culinary Walking Tour tastings (smoked meat, poutine bites, Quebec cheese samples).
meals.dinner: Dinette Triple Crown on Notre-Dame Street West — a beloved mid-range spot known for fried chicken, craft beer, and a lively local atmosphere. Budget ~$30–40 CAD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Flight arrives at 13:00 — allow 1.5–2 hours for baggage, transit, and hotel check-in before starting the afternoon tour. Book the culinary walking tour in advance as July slots fill quickly. Wear comfortable walking shoes for cobblestones.

day_by_day.morning: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour: Take the metro (Orange Line, Jean-Talon station) to one of North America's largest open-air markets. Sample fresh Quebec cheeses, maple products, seasonal fruits, artisan charcuterie, and local pastries. Arrive early (~9:30 AM) for the best atmosphere and freshest produce.
day_by_day.afternoon: St-Laurent Boulevard Street Food Crawl: Make your way to the iconic 'Main' boulevard and spend the afternoon grazing through its diverse culinary landscape — Portuguese grilled chicken at Romados, Montreal-style hot dogs, Middle Eastern shawarma, and local dessert shops. Browse boutiques and soak up the multicultural energy of this legendary street.
day_by_day.evening: Just for Laughs Festival Experience: Head to the Quartier des Spectacles for the Just for Laughs Festival (running mid-July 2027). Enjoy free outdoor performances, comedy street acts, and live music on the outdoor stages. The festival atmosphere is electric with food vendors and crowds of locals.

meals.breakfast: At Jean-Talon Market — grab a fresh pastry and café au lait from one of the market's bakery stalls. Budget ~$8–12 CAD.
meals.lunch: St-Laurent Boulevard Street Food Crawl tastings serve as lunch — Portuguese chicken, a smoked meat sandwich, or a falafel wrap. Budget ~$15–20 CAD.
meals.dinner: Schwartz's Deli on St-Laurent — the legendary Montreal smoked meat institution. Expect a short queue; it's worth it. Budget ~$20–25 CAD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Jean-Talon Market is busiest on weekday mornings — a Thursday visit is ideal. The Just for Laughs outdoor shows are free; indoor ticketed shows are available for ~$30–80 CAD if you'd like to upgrade the evening. Check the festival schedule at hahaha.com for specific show times.

day_by_day.morning: Mont Royal Park Tam-Tams Drum Festival Preparation & Park Exploration: Take a morning hike or bike ride up Mont Royal. Rent a bike near the park entrance (~$15/hour) and cycle to the Kondiaronk Belvedere lookout for panoramic views of the Montreal skyline. Pack a light snack from a nearby dépanneur (corner store) for a scenic picnic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Mont Royal Park Tam-Tams Drum Festival: Head to the base of the George-Étienne Cartier Monument for the legendary weekly Sunday Tam-Tams gathering — note this falls on a Sunday this week (July 20), so enjoy the park freely today. Instead, spend the afternoon exploring Plateau-Mont-Royal neighbourhood: browse vintage shops on Mont-Royal Avenue, explore Parc Lafontaine, and soak up the quintessential Montreal neighbourhood vibe.
day_by_day.evening: Montreal en Lumière or Just for Laughs Festival Evening Show: Return to the Quartier des Spectacles for another evening of festival entertainment. On Friday nights, the outdoor stages feature bigger headlining acts and the food village is in full swing with Quebec craft beers and gourmet street food stalls.

meals.breakfast: Café Olimpico on St-Viateur in Plateau — a Montreal institution for espresso and fresh bagels with cream cheese. Budget ~$10–15 CAD.
meals.lunch: Picnic on Mont Royal — grab fresh sandwiches, fruit, and local cheese from a nearby Plateau deli or grocery. Budget ~$12–18 CAD.
meals.dinner: Le Filet on Clark Street — a mid-range seafood-focused restaurant beloved by locals for fresh Quebec fish dishes and natural wines. Budget ~$45–60 CAD per person. Reserve ahead.

day_by_day.notes: The Tam-Tams drum festival occurs every Sunday at the Cartier Monument — if your schedule allows extending your trip or adjusting, Sunday July 20 would be ideal. Friday evening festival crowds are large; arrive by 7 PM to secure a good spot near the main stage. Plateau-Mont-Royal is easily walkable or a short metro ride from Old Montreal.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning in Old Montreal: Start with a slow breakfast at your hotel neighbourhood, then explore the Marché Bonsecours (Bonsecours Market) interior for local artisan crafts and Quebec-made goods. Visit the Pointe-à-Callière Museum for a fascinating underground archaeological tour of Montreal's founding site (~$25 CAD entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Old Port & Canal de Lachine: Rent a bike at the Old Port and cycle the scenic Lachine Canal path westward — a beloved local activity on warm summer days. Stop at the Atwater Market along the canal to browse local produce, Quebec meats, and artisan foods. Pick up any last souvenirs or local food products to bring home.
day_by_day.evening: Final Farewell Dinner in Old Montreal: Spend your last evening dining well in Vieux-Montréal, then take a final evening stroll along the illuminated cobblestone streets. If the Just for Laughs Festival has a closing weekend event, swing by the Quartier des Spectacles for one last taste of Montreal's festival spirit.

meals.breakfast: Olive & Gourmando on St-Paul Street West in Old Montreal — a legendary brunch spot with creative sandwiches, pastries, and excellent coffee. Arrive early as lines form quickly. Budget ~$18–25 CAD.
meals.lunch: Atwater Market picnic — grab charcuterie, cheese, fresh bread, and local cider from the market vendors and picnic along the Lachine Canal. Budget ~$20–25 CAD.
meals.dinner: Garde Manger on St-François-Xavier Street in Old Montreal — a celebrated mid-range restaurant by chef Chuck Hughes known for indulgent comfort food and a festive atmosphere. Budget ~$50–65 CAD per person. Reserve well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Atwater Market is open Saturday mornings and is lively with locals — one of the best market experiences in the city. Lachine Canal bike rental is available at the Old Port Éco-Quartier station (~$12–20/hour). If departing on July 19, ensure your dinner reservation is early enough to allow for a relaxed end to the evening. Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if needed.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — arrival day. Flight AC lands at 13:00. Transfer from Montréal-Trudeau International Airport to your luxury hotel in Old Montreal via private chauffeur service. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your accommodations in the historic Vieux-Montréal district.
day_by_day.afternoon: Old Montreal Culinary Walking Tour: After settling in, embark on a guided culinary walking tour through the cobblestone streets of Vieux-Montréal. Visit iconic spots for smoked meat sandwiches, artisan bagels, poutine, and locally sourced Quebec delicacies. The tour departs from near your hotel, making it a seamless and luxurious introduction to the city's food culture with no transit required.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a leisurely evening stroll along the Old Port waterfront (Vieux-Port) to take in the golden-hour views of the St. Lawrence River. Explore the charming lantern-lit streets of Old Montreal before heading to dinner at a premier restaurant in the neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: No breakfast scheduled — mid-day arrival. Enjoy a light snack or coffee at the hotel upon check-in.
meals.lunch: Included as part of the Old Montreal Culinary Walking Tour — taste smoked meat, artisan cheeses, and Quebec specialties at curated stops throughout Vieux-Montréal.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Toqué! — one of Montreal's most celebrated fine-dining institutions, just minutes from Old Montreal. Chef Normand Laprise's flagship restaurant showcases the finest Quebec seasonal ingredients in an elegant, Michelin-caliber setting. Reservation recommended well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance through your hotel concierge for a seamless luxury arrival experience. The Culinary Walking Tour should be pre-booked; many operators offer private group options for premium travelers. Pack light layers for the evening — summer nights in Montreal can be breezy near the waterfront despite warm daytime temperatures.

day_by_day.morning: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour: Head to Jean-Talon Market — one of North America's largest and most celebrated open-air markets — for an immersive morning food experience. Sample aged Quebec cheeses, artisan maple products, fresh heirloom produce, charcuterie, and local pastries. Engage with passionate vendors and gain deep insight into Quebec's rich culinary heritage. A private guided tour is highly recommended for a curated, in-depth experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: St-Laurent Boulevard Street Food Crawl: Make your way to the iconic 'Main' — Boulevard Saint-Laurent — for an afternoon of diverse culinary exploration. Stroll from one renowned spot to the next, sampling Portuguese flame-grilled chicken, Montreal-style smoked meat, bagels, and international street food representing the city's multicultural identity. This legendary boulevard pulses with energy, art, and flavor.
day_by_day.evening: Just for Laughs Festival Experience: Montreal's world-famous Just for Laughs (Juste pour rire) Festival runs throughout July, and this evening is your chance to immerse yourself in it. Enjoy free outdoor performances, live street entertainment, and vibrant festival street food along Rue Saint-Denis and surrounding areas. For a premium experience, upgrade to VIP gala tickets featuring internationally renowned comedians in an intimate indoor venue.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or at Olive & Gourmando in Old Montreal — a beloved artisan café known for its freshly baked pastries, pressed sandwiches, and specialty coffee. A perfect pre-market fuel stop.
meals.lunch: Light grazing lunch during the Jean-Talon Market Food Tour — enjoy a curated spread of Quebec cheeses, charcuterie, fresh fruit, and market-made pastries at the market itself. Supplement with a sit-down lunch at Pizzeria Gema (Mile-Ex neighborhood, near Jean-Talon) for award-winning Neapolitan pizza.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Monarque — an upscale brasserie on Saint-Jacques Street celebrating Quebec terroir with refined French-Canadian cuisine, an exceptional wine list, and a stunning heritage interior. Ideal for a celebratory pre-festival dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Jean-Talon Market is best visited early (opening around 7–9 AM depending on season) to experience peak vendor activity and freshest produce — plan to depart the hotel by 9:00 AM. Book a private food tour guide for Jean-Talon in advance. For Just for Laughs, check the official festival schedule at hahaha.com and purchase premium or VIP gala tickets well ahead of travel — top-tier shows sell out quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Mont Royal Park Tam-Tams Drum Festival: Though the legendary Tam-Tams gathering traditionally takes place on Sundays, Friday mornings offer a peaceful premium experience at Mont Royal Park itself. Hire a private guide for a scenic hike or carriage ride through the park designed by Frederick Law Olmsted (designer of Central Park). Visit the Kondiaronk Belvedere lookout for breathtaking panoramic views of Montreal's skyline and the St. Lawrence River.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Plateau-Mont-Royal and Mile End neighborhoods — Montreal's trendiest cultural districts. Visit local art galleries, boutique shops, and street-art installations. Stop at the famous Fairmount Bagel or St-Viateur Bagel for a legendary Montreal bagel fresh from the wood-fired oven. Browse the vibrant Laurier Avenue for luxury local boutiques and design studios.
day_by_day.evening: Montreal en Lumière or Just for Laughs Festival Evening Experience: Return to the Just for Laughs Festival for another evening of world-class entertainment. Opt for a premium VIP comedy gala or an exclusive comedy club experience at Club Soda or Théâtre St-Denis. Alternatively, explore the outdoor festival village for live music, artisan food stalls, and street performances under the summer sky.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Hôtel William Gray's rooftop terrace (if staying nearby) or at Crew Collective & Café — a stunning café housed inside a grand Beaux-Arts bank building. Enjoy specialty coffee, avocado toast, and fresh pastries in an architecturally spectacular setting.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Lawrence Restaurant in Mile End — a beloved neighborhood institution serving outstanding seasonal British-influenced cuisine with locally sourced Quebec ingredients. Known for exceptional weekend brunches and lunches with a relaxed, premium atmosphere.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Le Vin Papillon — Joe Beef's acclaimed wine bar and vegetable-forward restaurant on Notre-Dame Street West. Celebrated for its creative small plates, exceptional natural wine selection, and convivial atmosphere. One of Montreal's most sought-after dining reservations.

day_by_day.notes: The Sunday Tam-Tams gathering (hundreds of drummers, dancers, and performers at the base of Mont Royal near the George-Étienne Cartier Monument) is a Montreal institution — if your schedule allows flexibility, consider swapping Day 3 and Day 4 to experience the authentic Sunday Tam-Tams. Pre-book all restaurant reservations at least 2–4 weeks in advance, especially Le Vin Papillon, which does not take reservations for walk-ins and operates on a first-come basis — ask your hotel concierge for assistance securing a spot.

day_by_day.morning: Mont Royal Park Tam-Tams Drum Festival (Weekend Edition): Begin your final morning with a private sunrise hike or guided walk through Mont Royal Park. On weekends, the park comes alive with local Montrealers enjoying outdoor activities. Visit the Beaver Lake (Lac aux Castors) area for a serene lakeside experience, and explore the park's hidden trails and scenic lookouts with a knowledgeable local guide who can share the park's history and cultural significance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Old Montreal for a final afternoon of luxury leisure. Visit the Pointe-à-Callière Museum — Montreal's archaeology and history museum built over actual archaeological ruins — for a fascinating deep-dive into the city's founding history. Afterward, browse the upscale boutiques and art galleries along Rue Notre-Dame and Rue Saint-Paul, picking up artisan souvenirs, Quebec spirits, or local artwork as premium mementos.
day_by_day.evening: Grand Farewell Dinner: Conclude your premium Montreal journey with an unforgettable farewell dinner at Joe Beef — arguably Canada's most famous restaurant, helmed by chefs David McMillan and Frédéric Morin. This legendary Little Burgundy institution offers a theatrical, indulgent dining experience with a menu built around the finest Quebec and French ingredients, an extraordinary wine cellar, and an atmosphere that is simultaneously rustic and refined. A bucket-list Montreal dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at your hotel or at Café Parvis — a chic, design-forward café in the downtown core known for exceptional specialty coffee, fresh-baked goods, and elevated breakfast plates. A perfect relaxed start to your final day.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Maison Boulud inside the Ritz-Carlton Montreal — Chef Daniel Boulud's celebrated Montreal outpost offers an exquisite French-inspired lunch menu in one of the city's most glamorous dining rooms, complete with a beautiful garden terrace perfect for warm summer afternoons.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Joe Beef (Little Burgundy) — Montreal's most iconic fine-dining destination. Indulge in the legendary lobster spaghetti, foie gras preparations, and exceptional charcuterie boards paired with selections from their world-class wine list. Book this reservation months in advance through your hotel concierge.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private chauffeur or luxury car service for any departure transfers on Day 5 (if flying out) through your hotel concierge before your last evening. Consider purchasing Quebec artisan products — maple syrup, ice cider, local cheeses, and smoked meats — from Jean-Talon Market or specialty shops in Old Montreal as premium gifts or personal keepsakes. Confirm all restaurant reservations 24–48 hours before each dining experience. Tipping in Montreal follows standard North American practice (18–20% at fine-dining establishments).
